missing_pieces.duty: MP-0(a): Supply in complete form, in the owned body and annex, BGG 1997 Sect. 2.1.2 Exercise 2.1.31 (book pp. 35-36; PDF pp. 42-43). Show that rho_{M,prec} can be chosen as a formula of the form forall x Zx and forall x exists u forall y phi. Here Z is a monadic predicate symbol, and phi contains no variables other than x, u, y and uses only the three binary predicate symbols H, T_0, K plus finitely many monadic predicate symbols. The source's hint: use the universality of Turing machines with binary alphabet {0,1}, read Zx as x=0, and incorporate START into phi as Zy -> START[0/y]. Give a written proof, and add the following Remark (forall y Hyy). No handbook file treats Exercise 2.1.31. The existing rho_{M,prec} (def:p02-w02-p02-036-refined) uses S, the prefix forall x exists u exists v forall y, and a binary T_a for each tape letter, so it is not of the required form. Items (b)-(f) of MP-0 are covered at body 91-667 and annex 12-902.

MP-1: B. A. Trakhtenbrot, 'The Impossibility of an Algorithm for the Decision Problem on Finite Classes', Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR 70 (1950), pp. 569-572 (ACQ-2026-10-0615) is not held. held-sources.json lists only the 1962 Siberian Math. J. article. Whether the duty applies at all is a scope question; the handbook's own proof (w02-p02-036 body 383-390 and its annex) is self-contained.

actual_declarations.text:
\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p03-fol-zero-one}{cited=Fagin1976}{FO zero--one law}
For every first-order \(\tau\)-sentence \(\varphi\), if \(\mathcal A_n\) is
uniformly random among the labeled \(\tau\)-structures with universe \([n]\),
then
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr[\mathcal A_n\entails\varphi]
  \quad\text{exists and belongs to }\{0,1\}.
\]
\end{hbtheorem}

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p03-fagin}{cited=Fagin1974}{Fagin's theorem}
Over finite relational structures, an isomorphism-closed property belongs to
\(\mathsf{NP}\) if and only if it is definable by an existential second-order
sentence.
